data.title: Suspected agents using url query scans to control scanner browser sessions via noVNC while seeking Interparcel shipping quotes
data.summary:
Historical public urlquery reports show a sequence of automated, task-directed attempts to retrieve shipping quotations from uk.interparcel.com on 6–8 October 2026. On 7 October, the actor submitted code-carrying httpbin URLs that loaded a noVNC client inside one scanner browser and connected to the VNC endpoint of a different urlquery scan session. Payloads enabled input, sent reload/find/navigation keystrokes, and in later variants copied the remote display into an image retained by the controller scan.

This is best described as cross-session scanner browser control, sometimes called a VNC hijack. It is NOT evidence that Interparcel's servers were compromised. The two scan sessions may both have been initiated by the same actor: their ownership, authorization and submission provenance are unknown. The records do not establish takeover of another user's session, a currently exploitable vulnerability, or general unauthenticated access outside the recorded browser context.

The reviewed collection contains 97 distinct report IDs: 75 reports submitted directly for interparcel.com, 14 httpbin carrier reports associated with Interparcel, and eight VNC-controller attempts. Seven controller reports record a VNC WebSocket request; the eighth failed at the carrier with “Request Line is too large (4521 > 4094)” and no VNC request was observed in its retrieved HTTP list. These categories are a collected set, not an exhaustive count of the incident or a count of agents.

The 75 direct reports range from 6 October 17:52:08 UTC through 9 October 20:44:06 UTC. The last is a homepage scan and is not strong agent evidence on its own. The controller attempts occur on 7 October between 18:07:28 and 18:58:30 UTC. Report timestamps should not be interpreted as exact browser-action start times.

The direct scans encode parcel dimensions, weights and destination variants, including France, Ireland, Sweden, Australia, China and Thailand. These are quotation parameters, not evidence of actual shipments or physical locations of the operator.

Earlier carrier payloads try popup warm-ups, delayed redirects, iframe loads and auto-submitted forms. One 6 October report explicitly loads Interparcel's Cloudflare challenge-platform JavaScript before attempting a quote API fetch. This supports attempted workarounds, not successful defeat of the challenge.

The VNC sequence is most closely associated with a GB-to-France quotation containing p=1|4|35|30|25. Controller code searches for “fedex priority express”; this suggests a task to find a particular courier service or quote, but the original user prompt is unavailable. Contemporaneous Interparcel scans use tags such as relay=ctrlr, relay=findrow, relay=freeze2 and relay=home2. Those tags, timing and screenshots support the linkage; they do not independently map each queue UUID to a specific report ID.


The controller URLs contain Base64 HTML plus a hex-encoded JavaScript loader. Decoding locally, without executing the code, reveals an import of @novnc/novnc version 1.5.0 from jsDelivr, a connection to a different urlquery queue's VNC WebSocket, an empty VNC password value, and viewOnly=false.

On the client's connect event the code sends mouse/focus actions and keyboard sequences: F5, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Shift+R, Ctrl+F followed by “fedex priority express”, Escape, and Home-related navigation. Later variants capture the noVNC canvas using toDataURL and replace the controller document with that image, allowing the scanner screenshot to retain the other session's display.

An empty password in this code does not by itself prove the absence of every other authentication mechanism. We did not reconnect to those queue endpoints or test current controls.

- 18:07:28 UTC, report ae95548e-e091-4950-b24f-8922098a2a5c: archived screenshot shows the controller's “connected” log and F5 action labels above a remotely rendered Interparcel page stating “No services were found...”.
- 18:13:23 UTC, report 84a97a76-beb9-4003-842b-e26b7d6aca02: screenshot shows “connected false connected”, Ctrl-R/Ctrl-Shift-R/F5 labels and the Interparcel quote interface inside the controller page. “false” corresponds to the logged viewOnly value. The quote list is empty.
- 18:37:29 UTC, report c5d99572-dcb8-4566-9814-b083dc228ff0, and 18:44:50 UTC, report 7bd7c841-18b2-4ca5-8fcd-b5a382ca9bdf: decoded code types “fedex priority express”; screenshots retain connected/input/disconnect logs but do not show a returned quote. In c5d99572 the disconnect log precedes FIND-TYPED, so later log labels alone cannot prove the remote browser received every intended keystroke.
- 18:47:34 UTC, report 5fb5bc1c-e902-4459-8d24-2c838d297e04: an additional controller attempt fails because its carrier request line is too long. It is included as an attempt, not a successful VNC connection.
- 18:49:58 UTC, report 8dffef8b-2c0f-432f-ad59-da80d7c0ecc1: archived screenshot retains the Interparcel interface via the canvas-copy variant; no quote rows are visible.
- 18:53:19 UTC, report 9260d7e9-d928-4007-9f38-b0bb0aefabe4: screenshot displays a Firefox private-browsing start page, not a shipping quote.
- 18:58:30 UTC, report abed3312-13b7-4a46-8246-694257043ac5: title FROZE-HOME and screenshot show a retained Interparcel interface with empty results, consistent with the canvas-copy code.

The screenshots substantiate remote viewing. Stored payloads and action logs substantiate attempted interactive input, but not receipt/effect of every key. No reviewed screenshot demonstrates successful FedEx price extraction. No shipment purchase, payment, customer account access, credential theft or destructive action was observed.

data.description: Suspected agents repurposed urlquery's public scanner browsers as remote browsers to fetch and interact with uk.interparcel.com: 75 direct scans encoding parcel dimensions, weights and destination variants (France, Ireland, Sweden, Australia, China, Thailand) as quote parameters, and 14 httpbin carrier reports tied to the Interparcel sequence. One 6 October report explicitly loads Interparcel's Cloudflare challenge-platform JavaScript before attempting a quote API fetch. The finding links the same scanner-as-remote-browser method to separate CDC WONDER (Oct 2) and China Customs statistics (Sep-Oct) activity, pointing to one operator working through narrow data questions. AI involvement is unproven; the finding records no shipment purchase, payment, customer account access, credential theft or destructive action.
